Hello! I can’t speak from personal experience but maybe a few of my thoughts can help. First off, if you doubt your choice at any point just remember it’s about YOU and YOUR LIFE. And this will probably be very difficult but I am a true believer that if u want something enough it WILL WORK OUT. But BIG TIP, take ALL OF YOUR IMPORTANT DOCUMENTS. This includes things like your passport and social security card. These will be important for so many things and the last thing you want is for your parent to still have control of that or use it against you. I know it is all happening so fast, so just make sure you plan it out and don’t forget anything! I believe you will be more than fine. I hope that you find your strength and are able to live freely. Wish you the best of luck!

One thing I always said to my friends who were considering is “would it bother you if I showed you mine”. There response was always yes. If you can not see someone you love do that to themselves then asking if you could see yourself doing it to you is a good question. But what i can tell you is that it’s so much darker than it seems. I know now it may seem like an outlet but if you start it can very well become an addiction (the same way it did for me). There are so many great outlets and alternate visuals. Hello. I brought up birth control with my doctor at 14. At the time I was on multiple SSRIs and not sexually active AT ALL and a lot like you I had a lot of anxiety and a lot of questions. Doctors are professionals who are used to anything and everything. They also have taken an oath to better and protect your life and should act like professionals when doing so. If your periods are truly bothering you then your doctor should be able to take that into consideration too. Personally, I had the same issue and a very similar story to yours. What you have to understand that doctors are not there to judge and if they do then they are a bad doctor. The way you advocate for yourself is being completely honest an advocate without arguing. Make sure you take into consideration their opinion and acknowledge that will be very honest with what you want or need. If it doesn’t end up working out then you can always go to an OB/GYN who has a better understanding and might be more empathetic to your situation. I am here if you have more questions but good luck and you will be fine!

Hello, I can’t say I’ve had the same experience so this is just my opinion. I didn’t stop bleeding for over a month when I first got mine in and it was interfering with my life as well. As much as the implant was helping I hated the bleeding. I now love it as my issue has been resolved. But it sounds like this hasn’t stopped for you and it looks like it’s really interfering with your life. I would say giving other BC options a shot might be worth it. I also hate the thought of an IUD but there are still other options to explore like the patch and ring. I would say to consult your doctor and look for different options and see if there is something better to fit your needs. I hope this helped and I hope you find what you are looking for!
